name: PostPlanify
description: Schedule social media posts to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Facebook, YouTube, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky and Google Business Profile from your AI assistant. Plan your content calendar, track analytics and reply to comments.
author: PostPlanify

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Get the authenticated user's profile. Use this to verify the connection is working or to get user context.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List all workspaces (brands) the user has access to. Use this to find workspace IDs needed for other operations like listing posts or social accounts.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Get detailed info about a specific workspace including its connected social accounts.

tools.name: list_social_accounts
tools.description: List all connected social media accounts across all workspaces. Returns account IDs, platform types (INSTAGRAM, X, FACEBOOK, LINKEDIN, TIKTOK, YOUTUBE, THREADS, BLUESKY, PINTEREST), and account names. Use the returned account IDs when creating posts.

tools.name: get_social_account
tools.description: Get details about a specific connected social account.

tools.name: list_pinterest_boards
tools.description: List Pinterest boards for a Pinterest account. Pinterest posts need one of these board IDs as pinterestParams.boardId.

tools.name: upload_media_from_url
tools.description: Download a file from a public URL and upload it to PostPlanify. This is the primary way to add images and videos for use in posts. Supports: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, MOV, PDF. After uploading, use the returned media ID when creating posts. Workflow: 1) Upload media, 2) Note the returned media ID, 3) Create a post with the media IDs.

url.description: Public URL of the image or video to upload

filename.description: Optional filename. If not provided, extracted from the URL.

tools.name: upload_media_from_base64
tools.description:
Last resort for small files: upload a file sent as a base64-encoded string. Prefer, in order: upload_attached_file for files the user attached in this chat (ChatGPT); create_upload_url + finish_upload if you can run shell commands (curl); open_upload_box to let the user pick files from their device; upload_media_from_url for public links. The file is stored exactly as received, without compression or resizing.

Max size: 7MB. Supports: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, MOV, PDF. Returns a media ID that can be attached to a post.

data.description: Base64-encoded file content (raw base64 or a data URI)

tools.name: upload_attached_file
tools.description: ChatGPT only: upload an image or video the user attached in ChatGPT. Other clients: use open_upload_box (user picks files from their device), create_upload_url (if you can run curl) or upload_media_from_url instead. Call it once per file; for a carousel, upload each file and pass the returned media IDs to create_post in carousel order. For public links use upload_media_from_url. Supports: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, MOV, PDF. Returns a media ID that can be attached to a post.

download_url.description: Download URL of the attached file

file.description: The file the user attached in chat

tools.name: open_upload_box
tools.description: Show an upload box in the chat so the user can pick files from their own device (images, videos or PDFs, up to 300MB each, up to 20 files) and put them in carousel order. Use this when the user wants to post files from their computer or phone that are not at a public URL. If the user already attached the files in this chat, do not ask them to upload again: use upload_attached_file instead (ChatGPT). Use the upload box only when the files are not in the chat yet, or for videos and files too large to attach. After they upload, the user sends a message with the media IDs in order: pass them to create_post in that order. Do not call other upload tools for those files.

tools.name: create_upload_url
tools.description: Get a one-time URL to upload a file from the user's device directly, up to 300MB (images, videos, PDFs). Steps: 1) call this, 2) POST the file to uploadUrl as multipart/form-data: every entry of fields, then the file as "file" (last), (e.g. curl -F "key=<fields.key>" -F "Content-Type=<fields.Content-Type>" ... one -F per field ... -F "file=@photo.jpg" "<uploadUrl>"), 3) call finish_upload with the uploadId to get the media ID. The URL expires after 15 minutes. Supports: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, MOV, PDF.

size.description: File size in bytes, if known

tools.name: finish_upload
tools.description: After the file was uploaded to the URL from create_upload_url, call this with its uploadId. Returns the media ID to pass to create_post. For a carousel, finish each file and pass the IDs in carousel order.

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: List media that can be attached to posts. With workspaceId, returns that workspace's media library (the files uploaded in the PostPlanify dashboard) plus files uploaded through the API/MCP. Without workspaceId, returns only files uploaded through the API/MCP. Both kinds of media ids work in create_post. Each item has a "source" of "library" or "upload".

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID. Needed to include the workspace's dashboard media library; without it only API/MCP uploads are returned.

tools.name: delete_media
tools.description: Permanently delete an uploaded media file by its ID.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description:
List posts with filters. Returns paginated results. workspaceId is required. Statuses: SCHEDULED, PUBLISHED, CANCELLED, RESCHEDULED.

Set includeMetrics to true to attach each post's latest performance figures (views, likes, comments, shares, engagement rate). Use this to compare how posts performed instead of fetching them one at a time. A null metrics field means no analytics have been collected for that post, which is different from zero.

includeMetrics.description: Attach latest performance metrics to each post (default: false)

tools.name: create_post
tools.description:
Create and schedule a new social media post for one social account. socialAccountId comes from list_social_accounts. mediaIds come from: upload_attached_file (files attached in ChatGPT), open_upload_box (user uploads files from their device, best for local files and videos), create_upload_url + finish_upload (if you can run curl), upload_media_from_url (public links) or list_media. Pass mediaIds in carousel order.

PLATFORM NOTES:
- Instagram: Requires at least 1 image or video
- YouTube: Requires 1 video and youtubeParams.title
- Pinterest: Requires pinterestParams.boardId (board IDs come from list_pinterest_boards)
- TikTok: Requires at least 1 image or video
- X/Twitter: Max 280 chars, max 4 media
- Google Business: topicType STANDARD (default), EVENT, or OFFER. EVENT/OFFER require eventTitle + startDate + endDate.

scheduledAt must be a future ISO 8601 datetime.

socialAccountId.description: The social account ID to post to

caption.description: The text content of the post

mediaIds.description: Media IDs to attach (upload first), in carousel order

boardId.description: Board ID (required). Board IDs come from list_pinterest_boards

xCommunityId.description: X Community ID to post in

shortenLinks.description: Shorten links in the caption with the workspace's connected Bitly account at publish time (ignored if Bitly is not connected)

utmCampaign.description: utm_campaign value added to links when shortenLinks is on

actionType.description: CTA button type (not for OFFER posts)

actionUrl.description: CTA button URL (required when actionType is set, except CALL)

eventTitle.description: Event/Offer title (max 58 chars, required for EVENT/OFFER)

couponCode.description: Coupon code for OFFER posts (max 58 chars)

redeemOnlineUrl.description: Redeem online URL for OFFER posts

tools.name: get_post
tools.description:
Get detailed info about a specific post including content, status, media, publishing logs, and its latest performance metrics (views, likes, comments, shares, engagement rate).

The `metrics` field is null when the post has not been published yet, or when no analytics have been collected for it. A null metric means no data was collected, which is different from zero.

tools.name: edit_post
tools.description: Update a scheduled post. Only scheduled posts can be edited. Only include the fields you want to change.

scheduledAt.description: New scheduled time (ISO 8601, must be in the future)

shortenLinks.description: Turn Bitly link shortening on or off for this post

tools.name: cancel_post
tools.description: Cancel a scheduled post. Only scheduled posts can be cancelled. Cancelled posts cannot be rescheduled; a new post is needed instead.

postId.description: The scheduled post ID to cancel

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Permanently delete a post. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: get_account_analytics
tools.description: Get analytics data for a specific social account. Includes account-level metrics (followers, following) and post-level metrics (views, likes, comments, engagement rate). Returns platform-specific data format.

tools.name: get_analytics_trends
tools.description: Get historical trend data for a social account: follower growth and engagement metrics over time. Returns daily snapshots for the specified number of days.

days.description: Number of days to look back (default: 30, max: 365)

tools.name: get_brand_overview
tools.description: Get an aggregated analytics overview for a workspace. Includes all connected social accounts with 7-day metrics (views, engagement, follower changes), top 10 posts, and daily view/engagement trends over the same window.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List comments and reviews synced from Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Google Business for a workspace. Returns top-level comments with author, text, platform, post context, and read/hidden state. Use this to triage an inbox or find a comment ID before replying.

socialAccountId.description: Filter by a specific connected account

unreadOnly.description: If true, only return comments not yet marked as read

tools.name: list_comment_replies
tools.description: Fetch the direct replies to a specific comment. Use the `id` returned from list_comments as the platformCommentId. For LinkedIn URNs, pass the raw value as-is (e.g. "urn:li:comment:(activity:123,456)"), without URL encoding.

platformCommentId.description: Platform-native comment ID returned by list_comments

tools.name: reply_to_comment
tools.description: Post a public reply to a comment on its originating platform. The reply is published immediately. Platform length limits: Instagram 2200, Facebook 8000, LinkedIn 1250, Google Business 4096 characters. Cannot reply to hidden comments. On success, the parent comment's `brandReplied` flag is set to true. For LinkedIn, pass the raw URN as platformCommentId, without URL encoding.

platformCommentId.description: Platform-native ID of the comment you are replying to

message.description: The reply text. Must fit the platform's length limit.
